capabilities: Plan weekly workouts as editable Markdown notes with a readable set/weight format
Log sets through guided rep-counting or timed-circuit sessions, including motion counting on phones
Track goals, personal records, a history heatmap and body stats computed from logged workouts
Browse an exercise library with images, videos and animated muscle maps
Record progress photos and custom voice count-ins stored as vault files
extras: The manifest carries the warning "This plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff." The README details network use (plan library on raw.githubusercontent.com, media from wger.de) and privacy behaviour: clinical markers and progress photos are excluded from exports, and an in-progress session is kept in local storage, not the vault.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to plan workouts, log training sessions or follow fitness progress, so trainees must keep that data outside the vault.

relations.evidence: Starter images are from free-exercise-db (public domain / Unlicense)
Some starter exercises link media from wger.de, licensed CC-BY-SA 4.0.
Settings → Playlists lets you save Spotify or Apple Music share links
Install the BRAT plugin, then Add beta plugin and enter RuanPienaarCode/Gym-Vault

summary: Workout tracker that plans training, logs sets in guided sessions, and tracks goals, records and body stats as plain notes in the vault.
